anomalies.observed: R1 is drawn as a 10 MΩ resistor between the VCC rail and the Q_PMC_GSD node, which is the gate/base drive node of the fan power switch (connected to Q1 and pulled low by Q2).
anomalies.expected: A pull-up resistor on a PWM-driven MOSFET/BJT gate node should normally be low enough to turn the device off reliably and quickly, typically in the 10 kΩ–100 kΩ range for this kind of fan-control switching; 10 MΩ is several orders of magnitude too weak.

evidence.quote: R1 10M connected between VCC and Q_PMC_GSD (sheet 1)
Q_PMC_GSD node is connected to Q1 and Q2 collector (sheet 1)

anomalies.impact: The fan power switch will turn off very slowly or may remain partially on, causing inaccurate fan-speed control, possible fan chatter, and poor noise immunity on the gate/base node.

parsed.summary: The schematic appears to contain a wrong-value anomaly: R1 is 10 MΩ on the gate/base pull-up node of the fan power switch, which is far too weak for reliable PWM switching.
